6.2.1.5 is the correct answer! This enzyme catalyses the formation of succinyl coenzyme A from succinate and coenzyme A. It has a molecular weight of 100kDa and is a metalloenzyme which contains Mn2+ as its active site. The EC number for all enzymes are in the format 1) Enzyme class2) Subclass3) Main group4) Subgroup5) Final subgroup Numbers 1-5 are each a single digit and start at 1. Therefore the first number indicates the type of reaction the enzyme catalyses. In this case, 6 indicates that it catalyses a transferase reaction. The second number indicates the type of donor the enzyme accepts. In this case, 2 means that the enzyme accepts one hydroxyl group as a donor. The third number indicates what type of group is being transferred. In this case, 1 indicates that a methylene group is being transferred. The fourth number indicates where the donor attaches to the enzyme. In this case 5 indicates it attaches to a nitrogen atom. The final number indicates where the acceptor attaches to the enzyme. In this case, 2 indicates that the acceptor attaches to a carbon atom. The overall result is therefore 6.2.1.5. Caffeine has a positive inotropic effect on the heart (positively affects force of contraction). This is because it inhibits the breakdown of cAMP which leads to increased activation of adenylyl cyclase which causes increased production of cAMP. cAMP activates protein kinase A which phosphorylates phospholamban which means that there is less inhibition of L type calcium channels. This means that there is an increase in intracellular Ca2+ concentration during systole which means that more troponin complexes are released from the actin filament causing a stronger contraction. This is particularly useful for the exhausted junior doctor as it will mean that he doesn't make any serious mistakes on his ward round. Lypolysis is the breakdown of fatty acids into glycerol and free fatty acids in the adipose tissue. It increases the availability of free fatty acid which are transported in the bloodstream as fatty acid-binding protein (FABP).
